lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: data trends and uncertainty

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A trip cost depends on miles traveled. Define x.

steps: Define the relevant quantities and assumptions.
State a conclusion with its limitation or evidence.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A service is modeled by C = 12h + 25, where h is hours. Which assumption supports this model?
choices: Every service has the same total cost.
The number of hours is always zero.
The hourly charge remains $12 for every hour.
The flat fee changes each hour.

items.prompt: A savings balance increases by $15 each week. Which model type is appropriate?
A model gives 9x + 8 = 26. What is x?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Two constraints are y = 3x + 6 and y = 9x - 48. What is their shared solution?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A rectangular design has side lengths 5 units and 12 units. What is its diagonal?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a data set, hours of screen time increase and hours of sleep generally decrease. What association is shown?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
